name: theme-toggle
description: Presentational light/dark toggle with accessible labels and sun/moon state.
designIntent: Theme persistence is app-specific (cookie, localStorage, server session), but the control is the same everywhere. ThemeToggle owns the button, icon state, and accessible label while the consumer owns storage and the actual class/attribute switch.

props.name: onThemeChange
props.description: Fired with the next theme when the user toggles.

props.name: labels
props.description: Accessible labels for the action that will happen next.

examples.title: Cookie-backed theme
examples.description: The consumer persists the theme; the component only renders and reports the next value.

examples.title: Custom labels
examples.code: <ThemeToggle theme={theme} onThemeChange={setTheme} labels={{ toDark: 'Dark mode', toLight: 'Light mode' }} />

antiPatterns.title: Don't let the component own persistence
antiPatterns.explanation: Theme storage differs by app (cookie for SSR, localStorage for SPAs). Keep persistence in the consumer and pass theme/onThemeChange.

antiPatterns.title: Don't use an icon-only button without a label
antiPatterns.explanation: The component always sets aria-label and title; don't override them with empty values.

accessibility.implementation: aria-label and title describe the next action, not the current state.
Native button, Enter/Space activation, visible focus ring.
Icons are aria-hidden; the button label carries the meaning.

compositionRules.relationship: Place in SiteHeader actions or the app shell header.
